verdict.rationale: Nix is a local package manager, so the only retention and deletion control in evidence covers local Nix store contents. The garbage collector safely deletes unused packages, and a community user reports enabling automatic GC to reclaim large amounts of disk. That gives users direct control over what stays on disk, but it is store housekeeping rather than a documented privacy posture. Missing for 10: any documented data-retention or privacy policy, explicit statements about what data (if any) leaves the machine via binary caches or remote builds, and configurable retention for generations or logs described in privacy terms.
